initial_requirements: California Department of Transportation District 11 needs to replace the aging I-15 Reversible Lane Control System application. Traffic operators should be able to open and close reversible lanes for peak periods and special events, observe field-device and overall system status, issue control commands, configure operations, and generate reports. Authorized users and connected transportation systems should also receive relevant operational data through controlled local or remote access.

slots.key: Preconditions before issuing a lane reversal command
slots.value: Operators need a clear, current picture of lane status, field devices, and whether anything is preventing the change before issuing a command; the system should also warn when the system or field devices are not in the right state and show enough context to explain why an action cannot proceed. They should only be able to open or close the lane when the system confirms the field devices are in a safe and expected state, when the relevant operational configuration for that period is active, and when there is no conflict, fault, or incomplete transition; otherwise the operator should be blocked or clearly warned before proceeding. The command should be rejected or delayed if the lane configuration does not match the allowed time window, if another control sequence is already in progress, if the system cannot confirm the devices are synchronized closely enough to proceed safely, or if there is a communications issue that makes status uncertain. The system should force a warning acknowledgment when the action changes lane direction, affects a peak-period transition, or is being done under degraded conditions, including when it would override an active sequence, when recovering from a communication outage, or when field devices are not fully synchronized. Special-event operations or any action outside the normal schedule should also be treated as requiring explicit acknowledgment of the deviation. For occasional operators, the screen should clearly show what action they are about to take, which lane direction or segment is affected, and what the current system and field-device status is before they proceed.

slots.key: Operational exceptions requiring operator intervention
slots.value: Operators need real-time status on the lane controls, field devices, communications health, and any failed or uncertain states so they can tell immediately whether the corridor is safe. During and after cutover, support should include somebody who can respond quickly and make sure traffic operations can keep control without guessing. The view should also show the current commanded state, the confirmed field state, any device that hasn’t responded, conflicts between the requested lane position and field-reported state, the time of the last successful update, and any active alarms or communication losses. Stale data must be very obvious and not blended in with live status; if a device drops off briefly or an update is partial, the dashboard should clearly mark it as degraded, time out the old state, and avoid showing it as confirmed if it isn’t current. If the system can’t confirm the state, it should make that uncertainty visible right away rather than trying to guess.

slots.key: Escalation path for unresolved lane control faults
slots.value: For cutover, support should acknowledge immediately and start working the issue right away if there’s any impact to lane status, device control, or operator confidence in the system. Anything affecting safety or leaving the corridor in an uncertain state needs an active response within minutes, not a normal ticket queue. Low-risk cosmetic or informational issues that do not affect operations may be delayed and routed to the regular support queue. Anything involving a live lane-control decision should stay on the urgent escalation path until it is clearly resolved. If the lane is still live and a quick traffic decision may be needed, escalate to District operations right away because they own the operational call; the primary support contact stays engaged to diagnose and stabilize, but does not make the traffic decision. The vendor or integrator should be brought in when the issue looks like a system defect, field-device fault, or anything requiring technical repair beyond what District staff can resolve. If it’s clearly a minor operator-use issue and the lane state is stable, it can stay with the primary support contact without escalating further.

slots.value: A tested return-to-previous-state process, including the ability to suspend automatic actions, restore the last known good configuration, and reissue safe commands if needed. Automatic actions should be suspended when cutover produces any unsafe or uncertain condition, including loss of confirmation, inconsistent device status, failed command execution, or communications failure to a critical element. topics.topic_content: Rules governing when reversible lanes may be opened or closed

slots.key: Mandatory business rules for lane activation and deactivation
slots.value: Operators may open or close the reversible lane only when the system confirms the field devices are in a safe and expected state and the relevant operational configuration for that period is active. If there is any conflict, fault, or incomplete transition, the operator must be blocked or clearly warned before proceeding. Proper authorization is also required so only approved traffic operators can issue the commands. The command should be rejected or delayed if the lane configuration does not match the allowed time window, if another control sequence is already in progress, if the system cannot confirm the devices are synchronized closely enough to proceed safely, if communications issues make the status uncertain, if the command would override a currently active sequence, if the system is recovering from a communication outage, if the field devices are not fully synchronized yet, or if the action is a special-event operation or otherwise outside the normal schedule.

slots.key: Inter-stage support and fallback needs
slots.value: Between stages, communications links, field-device monitoring, and command capability need to remain in service or have a fallback so operators can still manage the corridor; support needs include real-time status on lane control command status, device position, communication link health, whether each field device is online, offline, or in an unknown state, timestamps for the last successful command or status update, event and fault logs that help locate whether the failure is in the application, network, or a specific field device, clear handling for safety-impacting or unresolved conditions, a simple audit trail or event history view to help operators and supervisors confirm exactly what happened during cutover and troubleshoot quickly, and a minimal status dashboard enhancement if it helps spot conflicting field states or incomplete commands before they become a safety issue. Anything that leaves lane state uncertain, a device responding inconsistently, or a loss of communications to a critical element should be flagged differently from routine alarms, as safety-impacting or unresolved rather than normal maintenance alarms. If something must be taken out of service temporarily, it should only happen with prior coordination, a safe fallback, and traffic operations aware of the exact impact. Operators would need to see the current commanded state, the confirmed field state, any device that hasn’t responded, any conflict between the requested lane position and what the field devices are reporting, the time of the last successful update, and any active alarms or communication losses. Stale data, partial updates, or a briefly dropped device should be clearly marked as degraded, timed out, and not shown as confirmed if current state cannot be verified.

slots.key: Role-based authorization for commands and data access
slots.value: Authorized users and connected transportation systems should receive relevant operational data through controlled local or remote access, and operational data must be shared in a controlled way so everyone who depends on it gets it when they need it. The replacement should also make it safer to coordinate with other transportation systems and authorized users, with better confidence in field-device status. Proper authorization is required, so only approved traffic operators can issue open/close commands. In normal day-to-day operations, operators can issue lane open or close commands after the usual login and role check without waiting for separate supervisor approval, provided they are authorized and system conditions are satisfied. For external sharing, only district-approved transportation partners and connected systems with a legitimate operational need should receive the data, under policy and access management, and the exact authorized list must be verified against the district and current integration agreements because it may change over time.
